revision_note: pin to the resolved commit hash after the first successful load, for reproducibility
lora_targets_note: standard Qwen2 dense attention projections; unlike Moonlight's MLA, Qwen2 has all four (validate against the live module tree on first load)

notes.why: Best-for-ethical-hacking candidate vs the frozen Moonlight baseline. Security work is code-heavy (reverse engineering, exploit/vuln analysis, code review, config, tool-output parsing) and Qwen2.5-Coder-14B is meaningfully stronger there than a general 14B, while remaining a solid general reasoner. Permissive (Qwen rarely refuses security content) and Apache-2.0 — and unnecessary refusals are already handled by the capability_first policy layer at inference, so no jailbroken/uncensored model is needed.
notes.dense: DENSE Qwen2 arch — standard bitsandbytes 4-bit, no MoE patch, no custom tokenizer, no trust_remote_code. Moonlight-specific runner bits are no-ops on transformers 4.57.6.
notes.run: MODEL_LOCK=MODEL_SPEC.qwen25-coder-14b.lock.json python evaluation/run_secv3.py   (and --rag rag/index, and bridge/interpret_recon.py). Compare to the moonlight-baseline runs.
notes.note_on_best: 'Best' is what the benchmark MEASURES, not what I assert — this is a strong, reasoned candidate; the v3 run decides. Alternatives worth a run: the general Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct (more balanced), or a security-specialised fine-tune like WhiteRabbitNeo (verify its usage licence; specialised, more variable support).
